context.guidance: Move credentials and keys that protect Personal Data out of source files and configuration into a secret store or the runtime environment. Rotate any value that has already been committed, and exclude .env and key files from version control and build context. Restrict the secret store to the identities that need it, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for the systems that hold Personal Data.

value.fix: Remove the hard-coded signing material from source and configuration. Load the key from a secret store (for example, AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or Azure Key Vault) or from runtime environment variables injected at deploy time. Treat the exposed value as compromised: generate a new signing key, rotate it everywhere it is used, and invalidate or re-sign anything the old key produced. Check git history as well as the current tree, because a committed value remains recoverable after it is deleted. Add .env and key-file patterns (for example *.pem, *.key, .env*) to .gitignore and .dockerignore so they stay out of version control and build context. Scope read access to the secret to the specific service identities that need it, following Rule 6(1)(b). Add a secret-scanning check (for example gitleaks or trufflehog) to CI to block future commits of key material.
